Surat at-Talaq is Madani according to all scholars. It has eleven verses, or twelve verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period, and count the waiting period, and fear Allah, your Lord. Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality. These are the limits of Allah, and whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has certainly wronged himself. You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter.﴾ (1)

It contains fourteen issues. The first: the words of the Most High: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾

The address is to the Prophet ﷺ, and he was addressed in the plural form out of honour and magnification. In the Sunan of Ibn Majah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divorced Hafsah, may Allah be pleased with her, and then took her back. Qatadah narrated from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ divorced Hafsah, may Allah be pleased with her, so she went to her family, and Allah the Most High revealed to him: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period﴾. It was said to him: "Take her back, for she is devout, fasting often, and she is one of your wives in Paradise." This was mentioned by al-Mawardi, al-Qushayri and al-Tha'labi. Al-Qushayri added: And in connection with her going out to her family, the words of the Most High were revealed: ﴿Do not expel them from their houses﴾.

Al-Kalbi said: The occasion of the revelation of this verse was that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry with Hafsah, because he had confided a matter to her and she disclosed it to Aisha, so he divorced her with one divorce, and the verse was revealed.

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Umar, who divorced his wife while she was menstruating, with one divorce. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him to take her back, then keep her until she becomes pure, then menstruates, then becomes pure again; then, if he wishes to divorce her, he should divorce her when she is pure, before intercourse with her. That is the waiting period by which Allah the Most High commanded that women be divorced. It was also said that men did the same as Abdullah ibn Umar did, among them Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, Amr ibn Sa'id ibn al-As, and Utbah ibn Ghazwan, and the verse was revealed concerning them.

Ibn al-Arabi said: All of this, even if it is not sound, the first view is the better. The most correct view concerning it is that it is an explanation of a newly begun legislation. It has also been said that it is an address to the Prophet ﷺ while the intended audience is his community. The two wordings alternate between second person and third person, and that is an eloquent usage, as He said: ﴿Until when you are in the ships and they sail with them by a good wind﴾ [Yunus: 22]. Its implied meaning is: "O Prophet, say to them: When you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period." This is the view of those who say the address is to him alone while the meaning includes him and the believers. And when Allah intends the address to the believers, He honours them by saying: "O Prophet." But when the address is entirely to him in both wording and meaning, He says: "O Messenger."

I say: The revelation of the ʿiddah (the waiting period a divorced woman must observe) concerning Asmaa bint Yazid ibn al-Sakan al-Ansariyyah supports the correctness of this view. In the Book of Abu Dawud, she reports that she was divorced during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, and a divorced woman had no ʿiddah at that time. So when Asmaa was divorced, Allah the Exalted revealed the ʿiddah for divorce, and she was the first woman for whom the ʿiddah of divorce was revealed.

It was also said that the intended meaning is the address to the Prophet ﷺ as an act of honour, and then He began, saying: ﴿When you divorce women﴾, like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone alters, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 90], and the rest of the verse [see vol. 6, p. 285]. Thus He addressed the believers as a way of giving them precedence and honour, and then He opened with: ﴿Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone alters, and divining arrows are...﴾, and the rest of the verse.

The second matter: Al-Tha'labi related from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Among the most hated of lawful things to Allah, the Exalted, is divorce." And from ʿAli, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Marry, and do not divorce, for divorce makes the Throne tremble." And from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not divorce women except because of a reason, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not love those who frequently taste [marriage] or the women who frequently taste it." And from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No one swears by divorce or makes another swear by it except a hypocrite." Al-Tha'labi, may Allah have mercy on him, traced all of these with their chains in his book.

Al-Daraqutni related: Abu al-ʿAbbas Muhammad ibn Musa ibn ʿAli al-Dulabi and Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, both saying: al-Hasan ibn ʿArafah narrated to us, saying: Ismaʿil ibn ʿAyyash narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Malik al-Lakhmi, from Makhul, from Muʿadh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "O Muʿadh, Allah has created nothing on the face of the earth more beloved to Him than emancipation, and Allah has created nothing on the face of the earth [addition from Sunan al-Daraqutni] more hated than divorce. So if a man says to his slave, 'You are free, if Allah wills,' he is free, and there is no exception for him. And if a man says to his wife, 'You are divorced, if Allah wills' [addition from Sunan al-Daraqutni], then he has the exception, and there is no divorce upon him." Muhammad ibn Musa ibn ʿAli narrated to us, saying: Humayd ibn al-Rabiʿ narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Ismaʿil ibn ʿAyyash narrated to us with its chain, similar to it. Humayd said: Yazid ibn Harun said to me: "What a hadith it would be if Humayd ibn Malik were known!" I said: "He is my grandfather." Yazid said: "You have delighted me, you have delighted me! Now it has become a hadith." ʿUthman ibn Ahmad al-Daqqaq narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Sunayn narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Ibrahim ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: Humayd ibn Malik al-Lakhmi narrated to us, saying: Makhul narrated to us, from Malik ibn Yukhamir, from Muʿadh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah has made nothing lawful that is more hated to Him than divorce. So whoever divorces and makes an exception, then he has his exception."

Ibn al-Mundhir said: They differed regarding making an exception (istithna') in divorce and manumission. One group said: That is permissible, and this view has been related to us from Tawus. Hammad al-Kufi, al-Shafiʿi, Abu Thawr, and the people of opinion (ahl al-ra'y) also said so. Making an exception in divorce is not permissible according to Malik and al-Awza'i. This is the view of Qatadah regarding divorce specifically. Ibn al-Mundhir said: I hold the first view.

The third matter: Al-Daraqutni related from the hadith of ʿAbd al-Razzaq, who said: My paternal uncle Wahb ibn Nafiʿ informed me, saying: I heard ʿIkrimah narrating from Ibn ʿAbbas, saying: "Divorce is of four kinds: two are lawful and two are unlawful. As for the lawful: that he divorces her while she is in a state of purity without having had intercourse with her, and that he divorces her while she is pregnant and her pregnancy is evident. As for the unlawful: that he divorces her while she is menstruating, or that he divorces her at the time of intercourse, not knowing whether the womb has conceived a child or not."

The fourth matter: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So divorce them for their ʿiddah﴾. In the Book of Abu Dawud, from Asmaa bint Yazid ibn al-Sakan al-Ansariyyah, that she was divorced during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, and a divorced woman had no ʿiddah at that time. So when Asmaa was divorced, Allah, Glorified is He, revealed the ʿiddah for divorce, and she was the first woman for whom the ʿiddah of divorce was revealed. This has already been mentioned.

The fifth matter: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿for their ʿiddah﴾ implies that they are the wives who have been consummated, because those not yet consummated were excluded by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then there is for you no waiting period [ʿiddah] to count against them﴾ [al-Ahzab: 49] [see vol. 14, p. 202].

The sixth matter: Whoever divorces during a state of purity in which he has not had intercourse, his divorce takes effect and he is correct according to the Sunnah. If he divorces her while she is menstruating, his divorce takes effect but he has erred from the Sunnah. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said, in another report [in the original: "in akhar", and both readings are unclear]: divorce does not take place during menstruation, because it is contrary to the Sunnah. The Shiʿah also adopted this view. In the two Sahihs, and the wording is that of al-Daraqutni, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, who said: "I divorced my wife while she was menstruating, so ʿUmar mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry and said: 'Let him take her back, then let him keep her until she menstruates a fresh menstruation apart from the menstruation in which he divorced her. If it occurs to him to divorce her, then let him divorce her while she is pure from her menstruation before he touches her. That is the divorce for the ʿiddah, as Allah commanded.'" ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar had divorced her with one pronouncement, and it was counted from her divorces, and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar took her back as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had commanded him. In a report from Ibn ʿUmar, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It is one." This is an explicit text, and it refutes the Shiʿah in their view.

The seventh matter: From ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The divorce of the Sunnah is that he divorces her with one pronouncement in every state of purity. When the last of that occurs, that is the ʿiddah which Allah, the Exalted, has commanded." Al-Daraqutni related it from al-A'mash, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbd Allah.

Our scholars said: The divorce of the Sunnah is that which gathers seven conditions: that he divorces her with one pronouncement; that she is one who menstruates; that it is during a state of purity; that he has not had intercourse with her in that purity; that no divorce preceded it during a menstruation; that no divorce follows it in a subsequent purity; and that it is free of compensation (ʿiwad). These seven conditions are from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar mentioned earlier.

Al-Shafiʿi said: The divorce of the Sunnah is that he divorces her in every state of purity specifically, and if he divorces her three times in one purity, it is not an innovation (bidʿah). Abu Hanifah said: The divorce of the Sunnah is that he divorces her one pronouncement in each state of purity. Al-Sha'bi said: It is permissible for him to divorce her during a purity in which he has had intercourse with her.

Our scholars said: He divorces her with one pronouncement in a state of purity in which he has not touched her, and no divorce follows it during the ʿiddah, and the purity is not directly after a menstruation in which a divorce took place. This is due to the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Let him take her back once, then let him keep her until she becomes pure, then menstruates, then becomes pure again; then, if he wishes, he may keep her, and if he wishes, he may divorce her. That is the ʿiddah which Allah has commanded for women to be divorced by."

Imam al-Shafiʿi relied on the apparent meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So divorce them for their ʿiddah﴾. This is general for every divorce, whether it is one, two, or more. Allah, Glorified is He, in this verse, considered the time and did not consider the number. Likewise the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, because the Prophet ﷺ taught him the time, not the number.

Ibn al-ʿArabi said: "This is a neglect of the authentic hadith, for he said: 'Command him that he take her back,' and this refutes the three. In the hadith he also said: 'Do you see if he divorced her three times?' He said: 'She has become unlawful to you, and she has separated from you through disobedience.'" Abu Hanifah said: The apparent meaning of the verse indicates that the triple divorce and the single divorce are equal. This is also the position of al-Shafiʿi, were it not for his statement afterward: ﴿You do not know, perhaps Allah will bring about after that a matter﴾. This nullifies the inclusion of the three under the verse. Most scholars said likewise, and it is an innovation (badi') for them. As for Malik, the general wording of the verse was not hidden from him, as they say, but the hadith explained it as we have said. As for al-Sha'bi's statement that it is permissible to divorce during a purity in which he has had intercourse, the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar refutes it, both by its explicit text and its meaning. As for its text, we have already cited it. As for its meaning: since divorcing a menstruating woman is prohibited because it is not counted, then the purity in which intercourse occurred is more deserving of the prohibition, because the ʿiddah is not counted from it due to the fear of occupying the womb, and due to the menstruation that follows it.

I say: Al-Shafiʿi, regarding the triple divorce pronounced in one word, argued with what al-Daraqutni related from Salamah ibn Abi Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from his father, that ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf divorced his wife Tamadur bint al-Asbagh al-Kalbiyyah, who was the mother of Abu Salamah, three divorces in one word, and it has not reached us that any of his companions criticised that. He said: And Salamah ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us from his father that Hafs ibn al-Mughirah divorced his wife Fatimah bint Qays during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ three divorces in one word, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made her irrevocably separated from him, and it has not reached us that the Prophet ﷺ criticised him for that. He also argued with the hadith of ʿUwaymir al-ʿAjlani when he performed the li'an, when he said: "O Messenger of Allah, she is divorced three times." The Prophet ﷺ did not reject this from him. Our scholars have answered this in the best of answers, and its explanation is in another place. We have mentioned it in our book al-Muqtabas min Sharh Muwatta' Malik ibn Anas.

From Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and a group of the Successors (tabi'un): whoever opposes the Sunnah in divorce, by pronouncing it during menstruation or three times, it does not take effect, and they likened him to one who was appointed to pronounce the divorce of the Sunnah and opposed it.

The eighth matter: Al-Jurjani said: The lam in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿for their ʿiddah﴾ means "in," like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He is the One who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering﴾ [al-Hashr: 2] [see p. 1 of this part].

in the first part of the waiting period (al-hashr)... [Translation of the passage follows]

Note on the instruction: I was asked to translate this passage faithfully and to reply with the translation only, without commentary, so I'll deliver just that.

**Translation:**

i.e., at the beginning of the hashr. So His saying "for their ʿiddah" means "in their ʿiddah," i.e., at a time that suits their ʿiddah (ʿiddah: the waiting period). There is consensus (ijmāʿ: scholarly consensus) that divorcing during menstruation (ḥayḍ) is prohibited, and divorcing during a state of purity (ṭuhr) is permitted. This is evidence that the qurʾ (qurʾ: a term with the sense of both "menstruation" and "purity") means purity (ṭuhr). The discussion of this was already covered in *al-Baqarah* [see vol. 3, p. 113]. If it is said: the meaning of "so divorce them for their ʿiddah" is "at the onset (qubul) of their ʿiddah," or "at the beginning of their ʿiddah"—and this is the recitation of the Prophet ﷺ, as Ibn ʿUmar said in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and elsewhere—then the onset of the ʿiddah is the end of the purity, so that the qurʾ is menstruation [in ḥ, s: "purity"]. It is said in reply: this is the clear evidence for Mālik and those who follow his view, that the aqrāʾ (aqrāʾ: plural of qurʾ) are the periods of purity (aṭhār). Had it been as the Ḥanafī and those who follow him say, it would necessarily follow that one who divorces at the beginning of the purity would not be divorcing at the onset of menstruation, since menstruation has not yet begun. Moreover, the onset of menstruation occurs by the entry of menstruation, and with the ending of the purity the onset of menstruation is not realized. And if the onset of a thing were the departure of its opposite, then the fasting person would break his fast before sunset, since the night comes in as the day departs before the day has ended. Then, if he divorces at the end of the purity, the remainder of the purity is a qurʾ; and because part of a qurʾ is called a qurʾ, as in His saying, "The pilgrimage is in known months" [al-Baqarah 2:197], meaning Shawwāl, Dhū al-Qaʿdah and part of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, and by His saying, "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him" [al-Baqarah 2:203], while he departs during part of the second day. All of this has been fully discussed in *al-Baqarah* [see vol. 3, p. 1 and p. 112].

Ninth: His saying, "And count the ʿiddah," meaning regarding those who have been consummated with, since a woman not consummated with has no ʿiddah. He may take her back during the period of less than three (divorces) before the ʿiddah ends, and after it she becomes like any other suitor. She is not lawful to him after three (divorces) except after another husband.

Tenth: His saying, "And count the ʿiddah," its meaning is: preserve it, i.e., preserve the time at which the divorce occurred, so that when the conditioned term—namely the three qurūʾ in His saying, "And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three qurūʾ" [al-Baqarah 2:228]—has ended, they become lawful to husbands. This indicates that the ʿiddah is the periods of purity and not menstruation. It is confirmed and explained by the Prophet's ﷺ recitation, "for the onset of their ʿiddah," and the qubul of a thing is linguistically and literally part of it, unlike istiqbāl (facing) of it, which is other than it.

Eleventh: Who is addressed by the command to count? There are three views: first, that they are the husbands; second, that they are the wives; third, that they are the Muslims. Ibn al-ʿArabī said: "The correct view is that the one addressed by this wording is the husbands, because the pronouns in 'you divorced' and 'count' and 'do not expel them' all follow one system referring to the husbands. But the wives are included in it by attachment to the husband, because the husband counts in order to take back, and to provide maintenance or cut it off, and to house or expel, and to attach his lineage or cut it. All these are matters shared between him and the woman, while the woman alone is distinguished by other matters. Likewise the judge needs the counting of the ʿiddah for issuing rulings concerning it and settling disputes when they arise. These are the benefits of the commanded counting."

Twelfth: His saying, "And fear Allah, your Lord," meaning: do not disobey Him.

"Do not expel them from their houses": it is not permitted for the husband to expel her from the marital dwelling as long as she is in the ʿiddah. She may also leave for her own need, unless there is a clear necessity; if she leaves, she sins, and the ʿiddah is not ended. The revocable (rajʿiyyah) and the irrevocably divorced (mabtūtah) are equal in this. This is for the preservation of the man's water (i.e., lineage). This is the meaning of the attribution of the houses to them, as in His saying, "And remember what is recited in your houses of the signs of Allah and wisdom" [al-Aḥzāb 33:34], and His saying, "And stay in your houses" [al-Aḥzāb 33:33]; it is an attribution of residence, not of ownership. His saying, "Do not expel them" implies that it is a right of the husbands, and His saying, "nor shall they leave" implies that it is a duty upon the wives.

In the authentic hadith from Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh, he said: "My maternal aunt was divorced and wanted to harvest her date palms (jadd: cutting the dates from the palms), but a man rebuked her for going out. She came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: 'Yes, harvest your palms, for perhaps you will give charity or do some good.'" Recorded by Muslim. In this hadith there is evidence for Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Ibn Ḥanbal and al-Layth in their view that the woman in ʿiddah goes out by day for her needs, and only remains in her home at night. According to Mālik, it is the same whether she is revocable or irrevocable. Al-Shāfiʿī said regarding the revocable: she does not go out either by night or by day, and only the irrevocable goes out by day. Abū Ḥanīfah said: that applies to the widow, but the divorcee does not leave either by night or by day. The hadith refutes him.

In the two Ṣaḥīḥs: Abū Ḥafṣ [also said: Abū ʿAmr ibn Ḥafṣ] ibn ʿAmr went out with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib to Yemen, and he sent to his wife Fāṭimah bint Qays with a final remaining divorce, and he instructed al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām and ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿah to give her maintenance. They said to her: "By Allah, you have no maintenance unless you are pregnant." She came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned their words. He said: "You have no maintenance." She asked his permission to move, and he permitted her. She said: "Where, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "To Ibn Umm Maktūm," who was blind, where she would put her clothes and he would not see her. When her ʿiddah ended, the Prophet ﷺ married her to Usāmah ibn Zayd. Then Marwān sent Qabīṣah ibn Dhuʾayb to ask her about the hadith, and she related it to him. Marwān said: "We have not heard this hadith except from a woman; we will hold to the consensus (ʿiṣmah) upon which we found the people." When Fāṭimah heard Marwān's words, she said: "Between me and you is the Qurʾan. Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Do not expel them from their houses...' [al-Ṭalāq 65:1]." She said: "This is for one who has the right of return. What matter arises after the three (divorces)? How then do you say: 'She has no maintenance if she is not pregnant'? For what then do you detain her?" This is the wording of Muslim. Thus it is clarified that the verse on prohibiting expulsion and departure concerns only the revocable divorcee. Likewise Fāṭimah argued that the verse that follows only includes the prohibition on the revocably divorced woman leaving, because she is in a position where the divorcer may develop a desire to take her back as long as she is in her ʿiddah; so she is, as it were, under the husband's control at all times. As for the irrevocably divorced, he has no such right, so she may leave if some need compels her or if she fears for the security of her home, as the Prophet ﷺ permitted her that. In Muslim: Fāṭimah said, "O Messenger of Allah, my husband divorced me three times, and I fear that someone will attack me." He said: "He commanded her, and she moved." In al-Bukhārī, from ʿĀʾishah: she was in a desolate place and was feared for, so for that reason the Prophet ﷺ gave her permission. All of this refutes the Kufan's view. In the hadith of Fāṭimah: her husband sent her a divorce that was remaining from his divorce, which is evidence for Mālik and against al-Shāfiʿī. It is more authentic than the hadith of Salamah ibn Abī Salamah from his father, that Ḥafṣ ibn al-Mughīrah divorced his wife three times in one utterance, as previously mentioned.

Thirteenth: His saying, "Except that they come with a clear immorality" (fāḥishah mubayyinah). Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, al-Ḥasan, al-Shaʿbī and Mujāhid said: it is adultery (zinā), so she goes out and the ḥadd (prescribed punishment) is applied to her. It is also reported from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Shāfiʿī that it is abusive speech toward her in-laws (aḥmā), so it is lawful for them to expel her. It is reported from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab that he said regarding Fāṭimah: "She is a woman who was overbearing toward her in-laws with her tongue, so the Prophet, peace be upon him, commanded her to move." In the book of Abū Dāwūd, Saʿīd said: "She is a woman who stirred up people [fatanat al-nās]"—meaning she stirred people by relating her hadith that the Prophet, peace be upon him, commanded her to move from the house of her divorcer in a manner that caused people to err—"she was sharp-tongued [lasinah], so she was placed under the care of Ibn Umm Maktūm the blind man." ʿIkrimah said: in the codex of Ubayy it reads, "except that they act immorally toward you" (illā an yafḥušna ʿalaykum). This is strengthened by the report of Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥārith that ʿĀʾishah said to Fāṭimah bint Qays: "Fear Allah, for you know why you were expelled." Also from Ibn ʿAbbās: fāḥishah is every disobedience, such as adultery, theft, and abuse of family. This is the choice of al-Ṭabarī. From Ibn ʿUmar also and al-Suddī: fāḥishah is her leaving her house during the ʿiddah. The construction of the verse is: "except that they come with a clear immorality," namely by leaving their houses without right; that is, if she leaves she is disobedient. Qatādah said: fāḥishah is nushūz (rebellion), and that is when he divorces her on account of nushūz and she then moves away from his house. Ibn al-ʿArabī said: as for the one who says it is leaving for adultery, there is no basis for it, because that departure is the departure of execution and killing, and that is not an exception in what is lawful or unlawful. As for the one who says it is abuse, it is explained in the hadith of Fāṭimah bint Qays. As for the one who says it is every disobedience, he erred, because backbiting and similar sins do not permit expulsion or departure. As for the one who says it is leaving without right, that is correct. The meaning of the statement is: "Do not expel them from their houses, and they shall not leave in the lawful manner, except that they leave in transgression."

Fourteenth: His saying, "And those are the limits of Allah" [ḥudūd Allāh]: that is, these rulings which He has made clear are the rulings of Allah for His servants, and He has forbidden transgression of them. Whoever transgresses them has wronged himself and brought it upon himself to the place of destruction.

"You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that a matter" (amran). The matter that Allah brings about is that He turns his heart from hatred of her to love of her, from aversion to her to desire for her, and from the resolve of divorce to regret over it, so that he takes her back. All the exegetes said: by "a matter" here is meant the desire for return (raj'ah). The meaning of the statement is an incitement to divorce with a single pronouncement and a prohibition of three, for when he divorces three times he harms himself when he regrets the separation and desires to take her back, so he finds no way to return. Muqātil said: "after that" means after one or two divorces; "a matter" means the taking back without dispute.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 65, verse 2–3 (part 1 of 2):

[[See vol. 3, p. 155 and p. (118)]]

(﴿then retain them with kindness﴾) means taking them back with kindness, that is, with a desire (to resume the marriage) and without intending to harm them by taking them back in order to prolong their waiting period, as has been explained earlier in "al-Baqarah." [[See vol. 3, p. 155 and p. (118)]]

(﴿or part from them with kindness﴾) means leave them until their waiting period ends, whereupon they gain control over themselves. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When they have reached their term﴾ implies that the word of the woman is to be accepted regarding the end of the waiting period if she claims it, as we explained in surah "al-Baqarah" at His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs﴾ [al-Baqarah: 228], and so on. [[See vol. 3, p. 155 and p. (118)]]

It was also said: the meaning is to call witnesses both at the taking back and at the separation. The second: According to most scholars, witnessing for the taking back is recommended. If he has intercourse with her, or kisses her, or touches her, intending thereby the taking back, and speaks of the taking back intending it, then he is a person who has taken her back according to Malik. If he does not intend thereby the taking back, then he has not taken her back. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: if he kisses her, or touches her, or caresses her with desire, it is a taking back. They also said: looking at the private part is a taking back. al-Shafi'i and Abu Thawr said: if he speaks of the taking back, it is a taking back. It has also been said: his intercourse with her is a taking back in every case, whether he intended it or not. This was narrated from a group of Malik's companions, and al-Layth held this view. Malik used to say: if he has intercourse with her without intending the taking back, it is an invalid intercourse, and he may not return to her intimacy until she has been cleansed of his invalid water, and he has the right of taking back during the remainder of the first waiting period, but he has no right of taking back during this cleansing period.

The third: Ahmad ibn Hanbal, in one of his two opinions, made witnessing obligatory in the taking back, and al-Shafi'i likewise, based on the apparent sense of the command. ﴿Allah has set for everything a measure﴾, meaning for everything of hardship and ease.

the term "أجلا" (ajalan) ends in a fixed term that it reaches. And it was said: "taqdiran" (a measure). Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 65, verse 4–5:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are in doubt, then their waiting period is three months﴾. In this there are seven issues.

The first: His saying, exalted is He: "And those who have despaired of menstruation among your women." When He had explained the matter of divorce and return (ruj'ah) concerning the woman who menstruates, and they already knew the waiting period of those who have menstrual cycles (dhawat al-aqra'), He informed them in this surah of the waiting period of the one who does not see blood.

Abu Uthman Umar ibn Salim said: When the waiting periods of women were revealed in Surat al-Baqarah concerning the divorced woman and the widow, Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: "O Messenger of Allah, people say that there remain among women those about whom nothing has been mentioned: the young girls and those who are pregnant." So the verse was revealed: "And those who have despaired..." up to the end of the verse.

Muqatil said: When His saying, exalted is He, was mentioned: "And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three menstrual periods" [al-Baqarah: 228], Khallad ibn al-Nu'man said: "O Messenger of Allah, what then is the waiting period of the one who has not menstruated, the waiting period of the one whose menstruation has stopped, and the waiting period of the pregnant woman?" So it was revealed: "And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation," meaning they have ceased from menstruation.

It was also said: Mu'adh ibn Jabal asked about the waiting period of the elderly woman who has despaired, and then the verse was revealed. And Allah knows best.

Mujahid said: The verse refers to the woman suffering from istihadah (irregular bleeding) who does not know whether the blood is menstrual blood or blood of an ailment.

The second: His saying, exalted is He: "if you are in doubt" — that is, if you are uncertain; and it was said: if you are certain. It is one of the words with opposite meanings (al-adda'), which may mean doubt or certainty, like the word "zann" (supposition). The preference of al-Tabari is that the meaning is: if you are in doubt and do not know the ruling concerning them. Al-Zajjaj said: "if you are in doubt concerning their menstruation, when menstruation has stopped for them and they were of the kind who menstruate."

Al-Qushayri said: In this there is consideration, for if we are in doubt whether she has reached the age of despair, we do not say that her waiting period is three months. The reckoning of the age of despair is, according to one opinion, the furthest customary age of a woman in the world; and according to another, the general practice of the women of the woman's kin.

Mujahid said: His saying "if you are in doubt" is addressed to the addressees, meaning: if you do not know what the waiting period is for the one who has despaired and the one who has not menstruated, then the waiting period is this. It was also said: the meaning is, if you are in doubt that the blood which appears from her is due to old age, or is the known menstruation, or is istihadah, then the waiting period is three months. Ikrimah and Qatadah said: "of the doubt" refers to the woman suffering istihadah, whose menstruation is not regular: she menstruates several times at the beginning of the month and once in the months.

It was also said: it is connected to the beginning of the surah, and the meaning is: do not expel them from their houses if you are in doubt about the completion of the waiting period. This is the most sound of what has been said about it.

The third: The woman in doubt about her waiting period is not to be married until she has cleared herself of her doubt, and she does not leave the waiting period except with the removal of the doubt. It has been said concerning the woman in doubt whose menstruation has lifted and who does not know what has lifted it: she waits a year from the day her husband divorced her, of which nine months are for purification (istibra') and three are the waiting period. If he divorces her and she menstruates once or twice, then it stops without her despairing, she waits nine months, then three months from the day she became pure from her menstruation, and then she is lawful to marry. Al-Shafi'i said this in Iraq. According to the analogy of this view, a free woman whose husband has died, after the nine months of purification, observes four months and ten days; and a slave woman, two months and five nights after the nine months.

It is also narrated from al-Shafi'i that her menstrual periods remain as they were until she reaches the age of those who have despaired. This is the view of al-Nakha'i, al-Thawri and others, and Abu Ubayd related it from the people of Iraq.

The fourth: If the woman is young, she is examined to see whether she is pregnant or not. If her pregnancy becomes clear, then her term is her delivery. If it does not become clear, Malik said: the waiting period of one whose menstruation has lifted while she is young is one year. This is also the view of Ahmad and Ishaq, and they related it from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and others. Al-Tha'labi said: This is the most correct position of the school of al-Shafi'i, and it is the view of the majority of scholars. This was also narrated from Ibn Mas'ud and his companions. Al-Kiya said: And this is the truth, because Allah, exalted is He, made the waiting period of the one who has despaired three months, and the one in doubt is not one who has despaired.

Ashhab said: she is like the nursing woman after weaning, by menstruation or by a year. Hibban ibn Munqidh divorced his wife while she was nursing, and she remained a year without menstruating because of the nursing. Then Hibban fell ill and feared that she would inherit from him, so he brought the dispute to Uthman, while Ali and Zayd were with him. If she is in doubt about pregnancy, she waits four years, or five, or seven, according to the differing reports from our scholars. The well-known is five years. If she exceeds that, she becomes lawful. Ashhab said: She is never lawful until the doubt has ceased for her. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is the sound view, because if the child can remain in the womb for five years, it can remain for ten and more than that. It has also been narrated from Malik something similar.

The discussion of this has already been fully given in al-Baqarah [see vol. 3, p. 174].

The matter has already been discussed in Surat al-Baqarah [see vol. 3, p. 174] and Surat al-Ra'd [see vol. 9, p. 284], and praise be to Allah.

Muqatil said: Whoever fears Allah by avoiding His disobedience, He will make for him ease in his affair by granting him success in obedience.

﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾, that is, acts in His obedience.

﴿He will remove from him his misdeeds﴾, from one prayer to the next, and from one Friday to the next.

﴿And will magnify for him a reward﴾, that is, in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 65, verse 6:

There are four issues in this. The first: the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Lodge them where you dwell, according to your means﴾. Ashhab reported from Malik: he (the husband) leaves her and she remains in the house, based on His words: "Lodge them." For if she were with him, He would not have said "lodge them." Ibn Nafi' said: Malik said concerning the words of Allah the Exalted, "Lodge them where you dwell," meaning the divorced women who have been separated from their husbands: there is no right of return (raj'ah) for them over these women, and she is not pregnant. Then she is entitled to lodging, but no maintenance (nafaqah) and no clothing, because she is irrevocably divorced (ba'in) from him; they do not inherit from each other, and he has no right of return over her. If she is pregnant, then she is entitled to maintenance, clothing and housing until her waiting period (iddah) ends. As for those whose husbands have not irrevocably divorced them, they are their wives and they inherit from each other; they do not leave (the house) unless their husbands permit them, for as long as they are within their waiting period. They were not commanded to provide lodging for them, because that is obligatory upon their husbands along with their maintenance and clothing, whether they are pregnant or not. Allah commanded lodging only for those who have been irrevocably divorced, together with their maintenance. Allah said: "And if they are pregnant, then spend upon them until they deliver their burden." So He made lodging and maintenance due to pregnant women who have been irrevocably divorced by their husbands. Ibn al-Arabi said: The elaboration and verification of this is that Allah, when He mentioned lodging, stated it without restriction for every divorced woman, but when He mentioned maintenance, He restricted it to pregnancy, which shows that an irrevocably divorced woman has no maintenance. This is a great issue, the paths to which we have prepared in the Qur'an, Sunnah and reasoning in the matters of disagreement. This is its basis in the Qur'an.

I say: The scholars differed concerning the woman divorced three times, in three opinions. The position of Malik and al-Shafi'i is that she is entitled to lodging but has no maintenance. The position of Abu Hanifa and his companions is that she is entitled to lodging and maintenance. The position of Ahmad, Ishaq and Abu Thawr is that she has neither maintenance nor lodging, based on the hadith of Fatimah bint Qays, who said: I entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with the brother of my husband with me, and I said: "My husband has divorced me, and this man claims that I have no right to lodging or maintenance?" He said: "Rather, you have the right to lodging and you have the right to maintenance." He said: Her husband had divorced her three times. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Lodging and maintenance are only for the one over whom the husband has the right of return." When I came to Kufa, al-Aswad ibn Yazid sought me out to ask me about this, and the companions of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) say that she is entitled to lodging and maintenance. It was narrated by al-Daraqutni. The wording of Muslim from her is: Her husband divorced her during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, and he had spent on her a meagre maintenance. When she saw that, she said: "By Allah, I will inform the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. If I am entitled to maintenance, I will take what suits me, and if I am not entitled to maintenance, I will not take anything." She said: I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he said: "You have no maintenance and no lodging." Al-Daraqutni mentioned from al-Aswad that he said: Umar, when the statement of Fatimah bint Qays reached him, said: "We do not accept the word of a woman among the Muslims." And he used to give a woman divorced three times lodging and maintenance. Also from al-Sha'bi, who said: al-Aswad ibn Yazid met me and said: "O Sha'bi, fear Allah and retract the hadith of Fatimah bint Qays, for Umar used to give her lodging and maintenance." I said: "I will not retract anything that Fatimah bint Qays narrated to me from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." I said: "How excellent this is." Qatadah and Ibn Abi Layla said: There is no lodging except for the one who may be returned to (raj'iyyah), based on the words of Allah the Exalted: "You do not know, perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter" (al-Talaq: 1), and His words "Lodge them" refer to what precedes it, which is the revocably divorced woman. And Allah knows best. Also, because lodging follows maintenance and runs in its course; so when maintenance is not due to the irrevocably divorced woman, lodging is not due to her either. The proof of Abu Hanifa is that the irrevocably divorced woman is entitled to maintenance, based on the words of Allah the Exalted: "And do not harm them to constrict them" (al-Talaq: 6), and withholding maintenance is among the greatest harms. Umar's denial of Fatimah's statement also clarifies this. Also, she is a woman in waiting period from divorce who deserves lodging, so she is entitled to maintenance like the revocably divorced woman; and because she is confined to him for his right, she deserves maintenance like a wife. The proof of Malik is the words of Allah the Exalted: "And if they are pregnant..." (al-Talaq: 6), as already explained. It has been said that Allah the Exalted mentioned the revocably divorced woman and her rulings at the beginning of the verse up to His words: "two just men from among you" (al-Talaq: 2), then after that He mentioned a ruling that covers all divorced women, concerning counting the months and other matters. It is general for every divorced woman, so the rulings that follow apply to every divorced woman.

The second issue: His words "from your means" mean "from your wealth." One says: "I found (wajadtu) in the wealth, I find (ajidu) wujdan, wajdan, wijdan, wijdah." And al-Wujd (the letter waw may be vowelled three ways) means wealth and capacity. The common reading is with a damma on the waw. Al-A'raj and al-Zuhri read it with a fatha, and Ya'qub with a kasra. All of them are dialect forms for it.

The third issue: His words "And do not harm them to constrict them." Mujahid said: "in the dwelling." Muqatil said: "in maintenance," and this is the view of Abu Hanifa. It is reported from Abu al-Duha: it is that he divorces her, and when two days remain of her waiting period he takes her back, then divorces her again.

The fourth issue: His words "And if they are pregnant, then spend upon them until they deliver their burden." There is no disagreement among the scholars regarding the obligation of maintenance and lodging for a pregnant woman divorced three times or fewer, until she delivers her child. As for a pregnant woman whose husband has died, Ali, Ibn Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, Shurayh, al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, Hammad, Ibn Abi Layla, Sufyan and al-Dahhak said: she is to be maintained from the whole estate until she delivers. Ibn Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, Jabir ibn Abdullah, Malik, al-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifa and their companions said: she is not to be maintained except from her share. Its explanation has already passed in al-Baqarah.

His words: "And if they suckle for you..." In this there are four issues. The first: His words "And if they suckle for you" — that is, the divorced women — your children from them; then the fathers must give them payment for their nursing. A man may hire his wife to nurse, just as he would hire a stranger; but according to Abu Hanifa and his companions, hiring is not permitted when the child is from them, as long as they are not separated (irrevocably); and it is permitted according to al-Shafi'i. The discussion of nursing has been fully presented in al-Baqarah and al-Nisa (already fully mentioned), and to Allah be the praise.

The second: His words "And let you consult together in kindness." This is addressed to husbands and wives, meaning: let each of you accept from the other what he has commanded him of the kind and good. Among what is good from her is nursing the child without payment; and among what is good from him is providing payment to her for the nursing. It was said: Consult together regarding the nursing of the child in kindness, so that no harm reaches the child. It was said: it means clothing and covering. It was said: its meaning is that a mother shall not be harmed through her child, nor a father through his child.

The third: His words "And if you disagree" — that is, over the payment for nursing, so the husband refuses to give the mother payment for her nursing, and the mother refuses to nurse him; then he has no right to compel her, and he should hire a wet nurse other than his mother. It was said: its meaning is "if you are constrained and quarrel, then let him seek another woman to nurse his child," and this is a statement in the sense of a command. Al-Dahhak said: if the mother refuses to nurse, he hires another for his child; if she accepts no one, his mother is compelled to nurse for pay. The scholars differed concerning who is obliged to nurse the child, in three opinions. Our scholars said: the nursing of the child is upon the wife as long as the marriage lasts, unless she is of high status, in which case the father must nurse him that day from his wealth. The second: Abu Hanifa said: it is not obligatory upon the mother in any case. The third: it is obligatory upon her in every case. The fourth: if he divorces her, she is not obliged to nurse him unless he refuses the breast of anyone else, in which case nursing becomes obligatory upon her. If they disagree over the payment: if she asks for the wage of her equal and the father refuses except as a voluntary gift, then the mother has more right to the customary wage if the father cannot find a volunteer. And if the father asks for the customary wage and the mother refuses, demanding an excessive amount, then the father has more right to it. If the father is unable to pay her wage, she is compelled to nurse her child.

There are four issues concerning this verse. The first: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Let the one of wealth spend from his wealth﴾, meaning: let the husband spend on his wife and on his young child according to his capacity, so that he expands upon them if he is of means. And whoever is poor, then according to that measure. Thus the maintenance (nafaqah) is determined according to the circumstances of the spender and the need of the one who is maintained, by independent reasoning (ijtihad) in line with the customary course of life. The mufti looks first at the measure of the need of the one maintained, then at the circumstances of the spender. If his circumstances can bear it, he enforces it upon him; if his circumstances fall short of the need of the one maintained, he reduces it to the measure of what he can bear.

Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, and his companions said: maintenance is fixed and specified, and there is no ijtihad for a judge or for a mufti in it. Its determination is by the state of the husband alone, in his ease and his hardship, and his wife's circumstances and sufficiency are not taken into account. They said: therefore what is due to the daughter of the caliph is what is due to the daughter of the guard. If the husband is wealthy, he is obliged to two mudd; if he is of middling means, a mudd and a half; if he is poor, a mudd. They cited His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Let the one of wealth spend from his wealth﴾, the verse. He made the consideration rest on the husband in ease and hardship, not on the wife. And because the consideration of her sufficiency, there is no way for the judge or anyone else to know it, which leads to dispute, since the husband claims she seeks more than her sufficiency, and she claims that what she seeks is the measure of her sufficiency. So we made it fixed, to cut off the dispute. The basis for this among them is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Let the one of wealth spend from his wealth﴾, as we mentioned, and His saying: ﴿The wealthy according to his means, and the straitened according to his means﴾ [al-Baqarah: 236].

The answer is that this verse gives no more than a difference between the maintenance of the rich and of the poor, and that it varies with the hardship and ease of the husband. This is granted. But that there is no consideration of the wife's circumstances in any respect, this is not in it. Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿And upon the father of the child is their provision and their clothing according to what is reasonable﴾ [al-Baqarah: 233]. That requires that what is reasonable be tied to the rights of both of them, since He did not single out either one of them in that. And it is not reasonable that the sufficiency of a wealthy woman be like the maintenance of a poor woman. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Hind: (Take what suffices you and your child according to what is reasonable). So he referred her to sufficiency when he knew the ease of Abu Sufyan's circumstances, which was obligatory upon him by her request, and he did not say to her that her sufficiency carries no weight and that what is due to her is something fixed. Rather he returned her to what he knows of the measure of her sufficiency, and he did not tie it to a known quantity. Moreover, what they mention of specification requires a revealed text (tawqif), and the verse does not require it.

The second: It is narrated that Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, imposed a stipend of one hundred dirhams on the newborn, and Uthman imposed on him fifty dirhams. Ibn al-'Arabi said: It is possible that this difference was according to the difference of years, or according to the state of the price-setting for the cost of staple food and clothing. Muhammad ibn Hilal al-Muzani narrated, saying: My father and my grandmother narrated to me that she used to come to Uthman, and he missed her. He said to his family: What is the matter with me that I do not see so-and-so? His wife said: O Commander of the Faithful, she gave birth last night. So he sent to her fifty dirhams and a shuqayqa of Sunbulani cloth [the shuqayqa: a diminutive of shiqqah, a type of garment; it is said to be half a garment. The Sunbulani (of garments): the ample, long one that hangs down. Sanbala his garment: when he let it hang down and dragged it behind or in front]. Then he said: This is your son's gift, and this is his clothing; when a year passes for him we will raise it to a hundred. Some of them regard it as recommended, because it falls under the ruling of the verse; and some regard it as obligatory, because of the new needs that arise and the expenses that come up, and I say likewise. Sufyan ibn Wahb narrated that Umar took a mudd in one hand and a qist in the other and said: I have imposed for every Muslim soul each month two mudd of wheat, and two qist of vinegar and two qist of oil. Another added: He said: We have granted to you your stipends and your provisions every month; whoever diminishes them, may Allah do to him such and such, and he prayed against him. As for the mudd, it has fallen out of use in favour of the kaylajah. As for the qist, it has fallen out of use in favour of the kayl. But the assessment for it, in our view, is two quarters for food and two eighths for condiment. As for clothing, it is according to customary measure: a shirt, trousers, and a robe in winter, and a cloak, a wrapper, and a mat. This is the basis, and it is increased according to circumstances and custom. The third: this verse is the foundation for the obligation of maintenance for the child upon the father alone, not upon the mother. Differing from Muhammad ibn al-Mawwaz, who says that it is upon both parents in proportion to inheritance. Ibn al-'Arabi said: Perhaps Muhammad meant that it falls upon the mother when the father is absent. The fourth: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it﴾, that is, Allah does not burden the poor as He burdens the rich. ﴿Allah will bring about, after hardship, ease﴾, that is, after constriction, wealth, and after hardship, abundance.

(They defied the command of their Lord), i.e., they disobeyed. He means the town, and what is meant is its people.

(So We called it to account with a severe reckoning), i.e., We requited it with punishment in this world, (and We punished it with a terrible punishment) in the Hereafter. It is recited with a light and a heavy pronunciation, and it has been discussed in the surahs of "Al-Kahf" [[note: what was discussed is in Surah al-Qamar, not Surah al-Kahf. See vol. 17, p. (129)]].

(So it tasted the consequence of its affair), i.e., the outcome of its disbelief. (And the outcome of its affair was loss), i.e., destruction in this world by what we have mentioned, and in the Hereafter by Hell. Then He explained this honour, saying: "a Messenger." Most scholars hold that the Messenger here is Muhammad (ﷺ). Al-Kalbi said: he is Jibril, and thus both would be sent down.

(Reciting to you the signs of God), a *na't* of "Messenger." *Ayat Allah* means the Qur'an.

(Clarifying). The reading of the majority is with a fatha on the *ya'*, meaning God has clarified them. Ibn 'Amir, Hafs, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read it with a kasra, meaning that it clarifies for you what you need of the rulings. The reading of Ibn 'Abbas and the preference of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim is the first, due to His saying: ﴿We have made the signs clear to you﴾ [al-Hadid: 17].

(So that He may bring out those who have believed and done righteous deeds), i.e., those for whom this was decreed in God's knowledge,

(from the darknesses), i.e., from disbelief,

(into the light), guidance and faith. Ibn 'Abbas said: it was revealed concerning the believers among the People of the Book. He attributed the bringing out to the Messenger because faith is attained through obedience to him.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever believes in God and does righteous deeds, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read it with the *nun* (we), and the rest read it with the *ya'* (He).

(God has indeed made good provision for him), i.e., God has widened his provision in the gardens.

Allah's words, "Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them" (Qur'an 65:12), indicate the perfection of His power and that He is able to resurrect and to call to account. There is no disagreement that the heavens are seven, some above others; this is shown by the hadith of the Night Journey (al-Isra') [see vol. 10, p. 205] and other reports. Then He said, "and of the earth the like of them," meaning seven. Scholars differed about them on two views. The first, which is the view of the majority, is that they are seven earths, layered one above another, with a distance between each earth and the next just as there is between heaven and heaven, and in each earth there are inhabitants of Allah's creation. Al-Dahhak said: "and of the earth the like of them" means seven of the earths, but they are closed upon one another without gaps, unlike the heavens. The first view is more sound, because the reports indicating it are in al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and others. This has already been explained in detail in "al-Baqarah" [see vol. 1, p. (258)].

Abu Nu'aym transmitted, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Hubaysh told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj told us, (ḥ) [it is the custom of the hadith scholars that when a hadith has two or more chains of narration, they write "ḥ" at the transition from one chain to another; it is a single unpointed ḥa', see the introduction of al-Nawawi to Sahih Muslim] and Abu Muhammad [in ḥ and s: "and Muhammad ..."] ibn Hibban told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Naji'ah told us, saying: Suwayd ibn Sa'id told us, saying: Hafs ibn Maysarah told us, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Marwan, from his father, that Ka'b swore to him by He who split the sea for Musa that Suhayb had told him that Muhammad (ﷺ) never saw a town that he intended to enter without saying when he saw it: "O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and what they shade, and Lord of the seven earths and what they carry, and Lord of the devils and what they lead astray, and Lord of the winds and what they scatter. We ask You for the good of this town, the good of its people, and we seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil of its people, and the evil of what is in it." Abu Nu'aym said: This is a sound hadith from the hadith of Musa ibn 'Uqbah; he alone transmitted it from 'Ata'. Ibn Abi al-Zinad and others narrated from him. In Sahih Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Zayd, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Whoever takes a span of land unjustly, he will have it hung around his neck from seven earths on the Day of Resurrection." Similar is the hadith of 'A'ishah. Clearer than both is the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No one takes a span of land without its right except that Allah will hang it around him to seven earths on the Day of Resurrection."

Al-Mawardi said: On the view that they are seven earths, one above another, the call of the people of Islam is specific to the people of the upper earth, and it does not bind those in the other earths, even if there are among them rational beings of discerning creation. Regarding their seeing the sky and drawing light from it, there are two views. The first is that they see the sky from every side of their earth and draw light from it; this is the view of those who regard the earth as spread out. The second view is that they do not see the sky, and that Allah created for them a light that they draw upon; this is the view of those who regard the earth as a sphere.

There is a third view in the verse, related by al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas, that they are seven spread-out earths, not one above another, separated by seas, and the sky shades all of them. According to this, if none of the people of this earth can reach another earth, the call of Islam is specific to the people of this earth; but if some of them can reach another earth, it is possible that the call of Islam binds them when it is possible to reach them, because the separation by seas, if they can be crossed, does not prevent the obligation of a ruling that is general in its application. It is also possible that the call of Islam does not bind them, because if it did bind them, the text would have come concerning it, and the Prophet (ﷺ) would have been commanded regarding it. And Allah knows best what He has kept to His knowledge, and the correct understanding of what is unclear to His creatures.

Then He said, "the command descends among them" (65:12). Mujahid said: the command descends from the seven heavens to the seven earths. al-Hasan said: between every two heavens there is an earth and a command. The "command" here is revelation, according to the view of Muqatil and others. Accordingly, His words "among them" refer to the space between this lower earth, which is the nearest of them, and the seventh heaven, which is the highest. It was also said: the command is decree and destiny; this is the view of most scholars. According to this, His words "among them" refer to what lies between the lowest earth, which is the farthest, and the seventh heaven, which is the highest. It was also said: the command descends among them through the life of some and the death of others, the wealth of some people and the poverty of others. It was also said: it is what He arranges within them of His wondrous management: He sends down rain, brings forth plants, brings the night and the day, summer and winter, and creates animals of diverse kinds and forms, moving them from one state to another. Ibn Kaysan said: this is according to the breadth and extent of the language, just as death is called "the command of Allah," and so are the wind, the clouds and the like.

"That you may know that Allah is over all things Competent" (65:12). Meaning: whoever is able to create this vast dominion is even more able to do what lies between them of His creation, and more capable of pardon and retribution, even though all of this is equal within His capacity and power [Qurtubi's note: his phrase "wa-mukntihi" means "wa-imkanihi," which does not appear in the lexicon books].

"And that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge" (65:12), so nothing escapes His knowledge and power. "Ilman" is in the accusative as an emphatic verbal noun, since "ahata" means "alima." It was also said: the meaning is "and that Allah encompassed with an encompassing of knowledge."

The surah is concluded, with the praise of Allah and His help. [What is between the brackets is missing from ḥ and ṭ.]
